name: Deva Simmons
bio: Deva Simmons is a No Party Affiliation candidate for Florida's 18th Congressional District in 2026, listed on the state's certified general-election ballot.
notes: Almost no public information found; the state candidate list is the only confirmed source.

name: Jim Schwartzel
bio: Jim Schwartzel is a Southwest Florida businessman who owns radio stations including 92.5 Fox News and Gulfshore Life Media, publisher of Gulfshore Life, Gulfshore Business and The Naples Press. He grew up in Fort Myers, graduated from Bishop Verot High School and attended Stetson University. He has not held elected office and won the 2026 Republican primary in FL-19.

platform.point: Finish the border wall, enforce immigration laws and stop illegal crossings and drug trafficking.
Keep taxes low and remove regulations he considers burdensome for small businesses.
Supports congressional term limits, arguing office should be about service rather than career.
Protect the Caloosahatchee River and area beaches through practical water-management policy.
Seek funding for road projects, septic-to-sewer conversion and a proposed interstate bypass through Immokalee.
Opposes DEI mandates and gender ideology in schools and transgender women competing in women's sports.

economy.evidence: Pledges to keep taxes low and eliminate regulations he views as burdensome, and opposes expanded federal spending.

liberty.evidence: Guns and LGBTQ issues: backs the right to bear arms, opposes gender ideology in schools and transgender women in women's sports.

immigration.evidence: Calls for completing the border wall and enforcing immigration laws, and backs continued deportation enforcement.

energy.evidence: Lists restoring energy independence under the America First agenda as a priority while opposing what he calls environmental extremists.

notes: Economy, liberty and energy scores are new and based on his campaign priorities page.

name: Victor Arias
bio: Victor Arias is a Cape Coral attorney who has run his own law practice since 2003, after moving to Southwest Florida in 1999 to work as counsel for the School District of Lee County. He was born in the Dominican Republic and raised in New York. He won the 2026 Democratic primary in FL-19.

platform.point: Bring down grocery and gasoline prices and back legislation to raise workers' earnings.
Improve environmental stewardship and protect clean water that the regional economy relies on.
Reduce bureaucratic obstacles veterans face in getting services.
Protect Medicare for seniors.
Encourage cooperation among counties to support recovery and the tourism economy.

notes: His campaign site was unavailable when checked, so the veterans and Medicare items come from its search listing. His stated goals are too general to score.

name: Seth Haskin
bio: Seth Haskin is a No Party Affiliation candidate for Florida's 19th Congressional District in 2026, listed on the state's certified general-election ballot.
notes: Almost no public information found; the state candidate list is the only confirmed source.

name: Debbie Wasserman Schultz
bio: Debbie Wasserman Schultz has served in the U.S. House since 2005 and chaired the Democratic National Committee from 2011 to 2016. She previously served in the Florida House and Florida Senate. Born in Queens, New York, she attended the University of Florida and is running in the redrawn FL-20 in 2026.

platform.point: Lists gun violence prevention as a priority and co-sponsored the STOP School Violence Act.
Supports security assistance to Israel, including 2023 military aid.
Opposes turning Medicare into private-market coverage for younger future retirees.
Criticizes ICE detention conditions and arrests of lawful immigrants.
Lists environmental protection and renewable energy among her official issue areas.
Makes breast cancer awareness and research a featured official priority.

economy.evidence: Record of Democratic economic votes, including the 2008 Emergency Economic Stabilization Act.

welfare.evidence: Supports the ACA and opposes converting Medicare to private insurance for future retirees.

liberty.evidence: Abortion rights and gun control on one side, but opposed Florida's 2014 medical marijuana amendment.

immigration.evidence: Condemned arrests of legal immigrants and called ICE detention conditions inhumane.

foreign.evidence: Voted for $14.3 billion in 2023 military aid to Israel and supported the Iran nuclear deal.

energy.evidence: Supports renewable energy and an offshore drilling ban.

tech.evidence: Co-sponsored the Stop Online Piracy Act in 2011.

education.evidence: Opposes school vouchers and backs public school funding.

notes: Security score removed because the cited summary gave no specific supporting vote or statement. No campaign site was confirmed.

name: Brent Andersen
bio: Brent Andersen is a businessman who campaigned on public safety, education and lowering insurance costs. He won the 2026 Republican primary in FL-20 over three opponents. He has not previously held elected office.

platform.point: Lower insurance costs by cutting red tape, pursuing tort reform and easing reinsurance treaties.
Made public safety a central focus of his campaign.
Named education as one of his three main campaign issues.
Challenged Rep. Wasserman Schultz to three public debates.

economy.evidence: Proposes cutting red tape and tort reform to lower insurance costs.

notes: Some coverage spells his name Anderson; the state ballot list uses Andersen. No campaign website was found.

name: Kedner Maxime
bio: Kedner Maxime is the Independent Party of Florida candidate for Florida's 20th Congressional District in 2026, listed on the state's certified general-election ballot.
notes: Almost no public information found; the state candidate list is the only confirmed source.

name: Brian Mast
bio: Brian Mast has represented Florida in the U.S. House since 2017 and has chaired the House Foreign Affairs Committee since 2025. He is an Army veteran who served as an explosive ordnance disposal technician and later worked for the Department of Homeland Security. He is originally from Grand Rapids, Michigan, and holds a Harvard degree in economics.

platform.point: Prioritizes Lake Okeechobee and water-quality issues affecting Florida's natural resources.
Strong supporter of Israel, framing that support as a human-rights and democracy issue.
Seeks to reduce taxes and federal spending to address the national debt.
Improve government care and services for veterans.
Protect Medicare and Social Security.
End federally funded animal experimentation.

economy.evidence: Voted for the 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act and lists lowering taxes and spending as a priority.

welfare.evidence: Supports repealing the ACA and voted for the American Health Care Act in 2017.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: opposes it with narrow exceptions; guns: backs an assault weapons ban and universal checks; drugs: co-sponsored the MORE Act.

immigration.evidence: Stresses legal immigration pathways and enforcement of the current system.

foreign.evidence: Strong backing for Israel but opposed additional Ukraine military aid in April 2024.

energy.evidence: OnTheIssues record summary leans toward fossil-fuel development, though he is in the Climate Solutions Caucus.

notes: Energy, tech and education scores rest on OnTheIssues summaries rather than specific votes found in this review; the security score was removed for lack of specific evidence.

name: James Martin
current_role: Coast Guard veteran and former White House national security aide
bio: James Martin is a fourth-generation Floridian from Hobe Sound and a U.S. Coast Guard Academy graduate who served ten years in the Coast Guard, including commanding a cutter in Fort Pierce. From 2021 to 2025 he served on Vice President Kamala Harris's staff as chief of staff for national security affairs and executive secretary. He won the 2026 Democratic primary in FL-21.

platform.point: Oppose tariffs, address corporate consolidation and widen capital access for small businesses.
Advance Everglades restoration, clean up Lake Okeechobee and stop harmful discharges.
Ban congressional stock trading, curb the lobbying revolving door and hold quarterly town halls.
Create a public option while keeping employer and union coverage, and rein in pharmacy benefit managers.
Pair border security with legal status paths, a time-bound asylum process and more immigration judges.
Oppose cuts or privatization of Social Security and veterans' benefits.

economy.evidence: Opposes tariffs, targets corporate consolidation and proposes tax incentives for employers offering benefits.

welfare.evidence: Supports a public health insurance option and opposes Social Security cuts.

immigration.evidence: Backs border security alongside legal status paths and an orderly asylum process with more judges.

foreign.evidence: Supports continued aid to Ukraine, while questioning Israel subsidies and opposing war with Iran.

energy.evidence: Prioritizes Everglades restoration and backs a possible St. Lucie Estuary national park.

notes: Facebook page is named on his site but its URL was not confirmed.

name: Alexander Cooke
bio: Alexander Cooke is a no-party candidate for Florida's 21st Congressional District in 2026, listed on the state's certified general-election ballot.
notes: Almost no public information found; the state candidate list is the only confirmed source.

name: Pia Dandiya
bio: Pia Dandiya is an educator who taught in public schools in low-income communities and became the founding principal of a public high school at age 28. She describes herself as the daughter of immigrants. She won the 2026 Democratic primary in FL-22.

platform.point: Lower housing, insurance, drug and childcare costs, and end tariffs she says raise prices.
Ban congressional stock trading and close the lobbying revolving door.
Protect Social Security and Medicare, reverse Medicaid cuts and have the wealthy pay more in taxes.
Fund universal pre-K, fully fund public schools and raise teacher pay.
Opposes repealing the Affordable Care Act.
Protect access to reproductive care and contraception.

economy.evidence: Calls for the wealthy to pay their fair share, an end to tariffs and action on price gouging.

welfare.evidence: Backs universal pre-K, reversing Medicaid cuts and keeping the ACA.

liberty.evidence: Abortion and LGBTQ rights: protect reproductive care and equal treatment regardless of identity.

education.evidence: Pledges to fully fund public schools and raise teacher pay.

name: Casey Askar
current_role: Chairman and CEO of Askar Family Office
bio: Casey Askar is a Marine Corps veteran and businessman who leads Askar Family Office, with holdings in franchising, commercial real estate, energy and construction. He immigrated to the U.S. as a child. He won the 2026 Republican primary in FL-22 after an earlier run for Congress in 2020.

platform.point: Cut taxes and regulations to fight inflation on groceries, gas and other essentials.
Repeal the Affordable Care Act while preserving Medicare and Medicaid and lowering drug costs.
Secure the border, deport criminal migrants and support law enforcement.
Expand domestic oil, natural gas, nuclear and coal production.
Require Real ID and citizenship verification for voting.
Counter China and fund the military under a peace-through-strength approach.

economy.evidence: Pledges to cut taxes and regulations.

welfare.evidence: Calls for ending the Affordable Care Act.

liberty.evidence: LGBTQ and parental rights: backs parental rights in schools and opposes transgender bathroom policies.

immigration.evidence: Calls for securing the border and deporting criminal migrants.

foreign.evidence: Backs peace through strength, military funding and countering China.

energy.evidence: Wants to expand oil, natural gas, nuclear and coal production.

notes: The 2020 run refers to the FL-19 Republican primary; no Wikipedia article on him exists.
